solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A short word, eg, may be one

definitions.text: A short word, eg, may be one

parts.words: A short word, eg, may be one
parts.note: a shortened form of a word, like eg for 'for example', is the very thing being described

explanation.surface: A brief remark about what counts as a short word.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue pretends to be about short words generally, but 'eg' is itself an example of the thing defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipped form of a word or phrase, such as eg, is the standard example of this term.

clue.text: Old and loose canine out at last

indicators.note: something let loose runs free, so the letters of canine are set free to rearrange
at last points to the final letter of the word out

explanation.surface: An elderly dog that has got loose and is finally outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges CANINE into ANCIEN; 'at last' takes T from 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient is a straightforward synonym of old, describing something from long ago.

clue.text: Throw out travel game

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it out
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Someone discards a travel board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a numbers game of chance played by calling and marking cards.

clue.text: Economist produced figures on screen

indicators.note: produced suggests the letters of Economist being made into something new

explanation.surface: The Economist magazine produced some statistics shown on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges ECONOMIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Emoticons are little faces built from keyboard characters and shown on computer and phone displays.

clue.text: Radio taxi carrying just a bit

indicators.note: the words Radio taxi carry the needed letters within them, across the word break

explanation.surface: A radio-dispatched cab carries only a small load.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota, the smallest Greek letter, idiomatically means a tiny amount.

clue.text: Hot-headed youth's rip-off?

definitions.meaning: a reckless, impetuous young person who causes trouble
read literally, to rip off is to tear something away

explanation.surface: Is a young hothead a swindle?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rip-off' suggests a swindle, but the question mark asks for the literal sense of tearing away; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is the British term for a wild, unruly young person.

clue.text: Where darts players stand is about right colour

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the darts line goes round the letter for right

parts.note: the oche is the line behind which darts players stand to throw

explanation.surface: A darts player's standing spot is about the right colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCHE is the throwing line in darts, a pub game popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment and the colour named after it.

clue.text: Developed sore knee getting fuel

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters of sore knee changing into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone's knee has become sore while filling up with fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developed' rearranges SOREKNEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerosene is paraffin oil, burned in lamps, heaters and jet engines.

clue.text: Short breaks in adult employment covered by note

indicators.note: covered by means the note wraps around the other letters

parts.note: PS is a postscript, a note added at the end of a letter
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
use means employment, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: Breaks in grown-up working life signalled by a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' puts AUSE inside PS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pauses are brief stops or intervals in activity.

clue.text: Groups of companies where no actor is trained

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters being schooled into a new shape

explanation.surface: Business groups where no actor has had any training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges NOACTORIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Consortia, plural of consortium, are associations of businesses working together.

clue.text: Animal that's holy without and venal within

indicators.note: without means on the outside, so the outer letters of holy are taken
within means on the inside, so the inner letters of venal are taken

explanation.surface: A creature that seems saintly outside but corrupt inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contrasts holy and venal characters, hiding that 'without' and 'within' are positional instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a scavenging African and Asian carnivore.

clue.text: Foreign divorcee gets zero credit in hearing

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
O is the shape of zero

indicators.note: in hearing means as the word sounds when said

parts.note: on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: A divorcee from abroad gets a zero credit rating at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' is informal British for buying on credit; TICK sounds like TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic describes something from a foreign land, striking because unfamiliar.

clue.text: Drunken sot found by shelter for poor people

parts.note: a haven is a place of shelter

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters of sot staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk is found at a shelter for the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' rearranges SOT into OTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The have-nots are those without wealth, in contrast to the haves.

clue.text: A sign of disapproval in case of treacherous restrictions

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the outer pair
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: boo is a shout of disapproval

explanation.surface: Booing in the course of some treacherous restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes TS, the outside of 'treacherous'; 'in' puts ABOO inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Taboos are social or religious prohibitions on certain acts or words.

clue.text: Flatter spread on unit prices, initially

parts.note: butter is a spread for bread

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of unit and prices

explanation.surface: Butter spread on bread with unit prices shown at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter someone up is an idiom for flattering them to win favour.

clue.text: Sloppy display of affection, hugging the French

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping round, so the caress goes around the article

parts.note: a caress is a gentle loving touch
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A slovenly show of love embracing the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless work is sloppy, done without proper attention.

clue.text: Person arriving in good time rarely bid freely

indicators.note: freely suggests the letters of rarely bid moving about without constraint

explanation.surface: Someone who seldom bids at auction does so without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges RARELYBID.
explanation.definitionFit: An early bird is an idiom for someone who arrives or gets up early.

clue.text: Divinely influenced tower in India

indicators.note: in places the tower inside the abbreviation

parts.note: IND is the international abbreviation for India
a spire is a tall pointed tower

explanation.surface: A tower somewhere in India.
explanation.walkthrough: IND is the international vehicle and country code for India.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspired originally meant breathed into by a god, so guided by divine influence.

clue.text: Saints, unusually, on a run, being skilled technicians

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the first piece comes after the second

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: unusually suggests the letters of Saints set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Saints on an unusual run of expert craftsmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means after, so the shuffled saints follow the A and R even though they come first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Artisans are craftspeople skilled in a manual trade.

clue.text: Sound arguments supporting a call to action

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means coming underneath, so the letter A sits on top
Sound means as spoken, so the word for arguments is said out loud

parts.note: rows are noisy arguments, rhyming with cows

explanation.surface: Solid reasoning that backs a rallying cry.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a row, rhyming with cow, is a quarrel; ROWS sounds like ROUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse people is to stir them, so the verb phrase call to action works as a synonym.

clue.text: Son's put on short pants

indicators.note: put on in an across clue means set after the other piece

parts.note: brief means short
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy has put on some short trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English pants are underpants, and briefs are a style of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are close-fitting underpants, which British speakers call pants.

clue.text: The misery of winter?

parts.note: seasonal affective disorder, abbreviated SAD, is a low mood brought on by dark winter months

explanation.definitionFit: Sadness is misery, and the question mark hints at the winter disorder abbreviated SAD.

clue.text: Partly covers surplus drinks

parts.note: over means left as surplus
laps means drinks, as a cat laps milk

explanation.surface: Leftover drinks only partly cover something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that overlaps extends partly over another thing.

clue.text: Delayed drinking last of hot coffee

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the later word goes round the letter

parts.note: late means delayed

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of hot

explanation.surface: Someone running late drinks the last of a hot coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' gives T; 'drinking' puts it inside LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is espresso with lots of steamed milk.

clue.text: Milk supplier backed by millions — countless!

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the word for milk supplier is read in reverse

parts.note: a dairy supplies milk

explanation.surface: A dairy supported by millions of countless customers.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'countless' look like an exclamation, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Myriad, as an adjective, means innumerable, from the Greek for ten thousand.

clue.text: Picture game played by head of Interpol

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of Interpol
played suggests the letters of game played around with

explanation.surface: A game played by the boss of Interpol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives I; 'played' rearranges GAME into MAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness of something.

clue.text: Part of Europe without one bridge

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Spain is a country in Europe
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A region of Europe lacking a single bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes I from SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is a bridge, or the stretch between its supports.

clue.text: Heads back with time to check growth

indicators.note: back means the word for heads is read in reverse

parts.note: nuts is slang for heads

explanation.surface: Heads turned back in time to stop something growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NUTS into STUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To stunt is to hinder or check the growth or development of something.

clue.text: Copy most of response that's protective of pet

indicators.note: being protective of something means guarding it, so these letters wrap round the pet
most of means the final letter of the word for response is dropped

parts.note: replies are responses
a cat is a household pet

explanation.surface: Reproduce a reply that shows care for an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter takes 'response' loosely as replies; trimming the last letter and wrapping the pet inside gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To replicate something is to reproduce or duplicate it exactly.

clue.text: Matching frock?

parts.note: matching here means joining in marriage, so this is a garment worn when a couple are matched

explanation.definitionFit: A bride's gown is worn at the ceremony where a couple are matched in marriage.
